title: Simulation Task
description: Develop a multi-agent simulation system that models the spread of mask-wearing behavior through social networks.
simulation_focus: Predict agents' mask-wearing behavior over day 30 - day 39 (last ten days) based on their attributes, social connections, and past behavior
Model information propagation and behavioral changes triggered by social influence and government intervention starting on Day 10

data_files.agent_attributes.csv: Contains demographic and behavioral attributes of each agent, including age, occupation, risk perception, and social connection counts
data_files.social_network.json: Contains structured data representing a social network. Each entry corresponds to a user (identified by a unique integer ID), and the values describe the different types of relationships that user has with others. Data Structure: The top-level structure is a dictionary ({} in JSON). Keys: Each key is a unique user ID (as an integer, e.g., 0, 1, 2, etc.). Values: Each value is another dictionary with the following fields: "family": a list of user IDs representing family connections. "work_school": a list of user IDs representing colleagues or schoolmates. "community": a list of user IDs representing community-level acquaintances. "all": a merged list of all user IDs connected to the user across the three categories above.
data_files.train_data.csv: Time series data for the first 30 days, used for training the model

RMSE.description: Root Mean Square Error measuring overall predictive accuracy of mask adoption rates
RMSE.interpretation: Directly interpretable as percentage deviations due to the 0-1 range

interactions.name: peer_influence
interactions.description: Individuals observe mask use and opinions of their social contacts and update their adoption propensity via threshold or weighted influence rules.

interactions.name: policy_enforcement
interactions.description: Authorities and locations enforce mask mandates, affecting individual costs/benefits and probabilities of compliance.

interactions.name: information_broadcast
interactions.description: Media and public health messaging reach individuals with varying credibility, shifting risk perception and norms.

interactions.name: location_norm_signaling
interactions.description: Observed mask prevalence at a location influences perceived social norms and immediate compliance.

metrics.name: RMSE
metrics.description: Root Mean Squared Error between simulated population-level mask adoption and observed adoption over time.

metrics.name: MAE
metrics.description: Mean Absolute Error between simulated and observed adoption time series.

metrics.name: MAPE
metrics.description: Mean Absolute Percentage Error of adoption rates compared to observed values.

metrics.name: R2
metrics.description: Coefficient of determination for fit of simulated to observed adoption over time.

metrics.name: AdoptionRateAtT
metrics.description: Population mask adoption rate at a specified evaluation day T.

metrics.name: TimeTo50Percent
metrics.description: Number of days until simulated adoption first reaches 50%.

metrics.name: PeakAdoption
metrics.description: Maximum adoption rate achieved and the day it occurs.

metrics.name: SubgroupDisparityIndex
metrics.description: Difference or ratio of adoption rates between specified subgroups (e.g., high vs. low SES).

metrics.name: RunToRunVariance
metrics.description: Variance of key outcomes (e.g., adoption at T) across replications with different random seeds.

validation_criteria.name: CalibrationErrorThreshold
validation_criteria.description: RMSE between simulated and observed adoption series is <= 0.05 (5 percentage points) over the calibration period.

validation_criteria.name: StabilityAcrossReplications
validation_criteria.description: Run-to-run standard deviation of AdoptionRateAtT across replications is <= 0.02 (2 percentage points).

validation_criteria.name: PolicyMonotonicityCheck
validation_criteria.description: Increasing enforcement_strength or campaign_intensity should not decrease aggregate adoption, all else equal.

validation_criteria.name: ConvergenceCriterion
validation_criteria.description: Further parameter searches do not reduce RMSE by more than 1e-3 over 20 consecutive evaluations.
